scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Dispute ticket volume: June 610, July 590, August 1180, September 1260

F-02.statement: Dispute ticket median response time 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days, total tickets 2440

F-03.statement: Route completion for Aug‑Sep 2026 is 0.88 vs target 0.95, with 9,200 manual read accounts

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-REQUESTER-FRAMING.statement: The requester's framing is correct: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

H-ROOT-CAUSE-UNKNOWN.statement: The operational root cause differs from the requested solution and must be established from data

interpretation_history.interpretation: The dispute ticket volume rose from ~600 in June/July to 1180 in August and 1260 in September, confirming the requester’s claim that tickets doubled since August and indicating a surge that needs root‑cause analysis.
Dispute ticket response times are comfortably inside the SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs 3.0 day SLA), showing that response speed is not the cause of the dispute surge.
Route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating a shortfall in field meter‑reading that could contribute to billing errors and the dispute surge.
Disputed bills occur for both read types, with more disputes linked to actual reads than estimated reads, indicating the issue is not limited to estimation errors.
No tariff change records were found, indicating that tariff changes did not occur during the period and are unlikely to be a driver of the dispute surge.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports a shortage of three field readers since July, causing routes to run late. This results in estimated bills for affected customers, potentially contributing to the dispute surge.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder asserts that there have been no tariff changes this year, indicating tariff changes are unlikely to be driving the recent dispute ticket surge.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract confirms that route priority changes can be requested by the utility but must be confirmed by the Field Operations Manager, aligning with the existing K-DISPATCH constraint that field dispatch changes require runtime confirmation by SH-FIELD.

U-ROUTE-IMPROVEMENT-IMPACT.question: Whether increasing route completion to target will sufficiently reduce estimated bills to lower dispute volume.
U-ROUTE-IMPROVEMENT-IMPACT.resolution_path: Run a controlled pilot improving route completion on a subset of routes, measure resulting estimated bill proportion and dispute ticket volume.
U-ROUTE-IMPROVEMENT-IMPACT.safe_placeholder: Maintain current staffing and route schedules while pilot runs; continue existing estimation process.

U-ESTIMATION-ACCURACY.question: Accuracy of the estimation algorithm for bills when reads are missing; whether improving estimation reduces disputes independent of route completion.
U-ESTIMATION-ACCURACY.resolution_path: Analyze dispute reasons for estimated bills to identify systematic estimation errors; test improved estimation models on historical data.
U-ESTIMATION-ACCURACY.safe_placeholder: Keep current estimation method; monitor dispute volume for changes.

U-HIDDEN-TARIFF-BILLING-RULE-C.question: Whether any hidden tariff or billing rule changes contributed to dispute surge despite empty log.
U-HIDDEN-TARIFF-BILLING-RULE-C.resolution_path: Audit billing configuration change logs and compare with dispute timestamps.
U-HIDDEN-TARIFF-BILLING-RULE-C.safe_placeholder: Assume no tariff changes; continue monitoring.
